html:
SMTO-OUT-0005 — Only part of this command's output was saved

GUID: ab0404b4-af42-483b-890a-9022c7321e89
Slug: shell-log-quota-reached
Domain: OUT · Subsystem: out

What happened

  • The command printed more text than SMTO saves for one step, so the rest of its log was cut off. The command itself still ran; only the saved log is incomplete.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If the command wrote its results to a file, open that file for the full results. A file keeps everything, while the log keeps only the first part of the output.
  2. For new work, ask the Agent to save large output to a file and show you only a short summary of it. Writing output to a file keeps it complete and keeps the log under the limit.
  3. Don't ask the Agent to run the command again just to see the missing part of the log. The command already ran, and running it again could repeat any changes it made.

What success looks like

  • You can open the complete results in a file, and new steps no longer say their output was truncated.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't delete the step's log; it still shows what the command did.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • ShellExecutor marked output_truncated because the command's stdout/stderr exceeded the per-operation capture quota (1 MiB of characters on the Server, or a truncation flag reported by the Gateway), and appended a truncation notice to stderr.

What this means

  • The shell output collector marks output_truncated after its configured capture quota is reached and adds a diagnostic to the result. Output extraction, rendering and summaries do not own execution truth. Their failure cannot turn a completed operation into unexecuted work or justify replay; retained exact receipts remain authoritative.

Why this can happen

  • The shell output collector marks output_truncated after its configured capture quota is reached and adds a diagnostic to the result.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect output_truncated and any existing complete file/artifact independently of the exit status.

How to fix it

  • Read exact deliverables from an existing output file or artifact. For new work, have commands write complete results to files and return bounded summaries; the Server cap is native_output_limit (1 MiB characters) in ShellExecutor._collect. Do not rerun a mutation just to reproduce its log.
  • Use an existing output file or artifact for exact deliverables. For new work, arrange complete results in files and return bounded summaries; do not rerun a mutation just to reproduce its log.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Exact deliverables come from retained complete files, with log incompleteness still disclosed.

What not to do

  • Do not erase authoritative receipts or protected current input to conceal a size/capacity problem.

Technical notes

  • Output extraction, rendering and summaries do not own execution truth. Their failure cannot turn a completed operation into unexecuted work or justify replay; retained exact receipts remain authoritative.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
